source.title: Lifted Representation Hypothesis in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neurons as one possible basis for reusable computation and reports neuron-wise activation-pattern measurements, but it does not test neuron interpretability, neuron explanations, or neuron-based attribution graphs as specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper’s empirical results concern generalization and revision on a synthetic modulo task, plus MLP activation-pattern similarity across task groups. The latter is recorded as related evidence, not as a test of the claim versions. The activation analysis uses cross-control distances as a reference; its figure values are not given numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper studies generalization and revision on a synthetic modulo task (NMR-Type) in LLMs. It does not test any version of the claim. It never audits neuron jobs, explains or scores neurons, studies InceptionV1, or builds neuron attribution graphs. Its MLP activation analysis compares group-mean neuron-wise activation vectors between task groups with a Mahalanobis distance. That is a related but different construct, not per-neuron interpretability. Neurons appear only as one cited candidate basis for reusable computation, alongside superposition and SAEs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Models generalize a broad modulo rule to a withheld subtype, then fail to localize its later revision, disturbing the parent group more than a disjoint control. The authors call this behavioral evidence consistent with the Lifted State Hypothesis and say it does not identify the representational or causal basis.
record.recipe_differences: The study’s synthetic generalization-and-revision task and neuron-wise activation-distance analysis are not the neuron audit, explanation evaluation, or attribution-graph method in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The activation-pattern relation varies by model and layer; the text reports relative convergence during W1 and reduced relative closeness after W2 begins, with layer-specific exceptions.

fits_no_version.finding: After W1, neuron-wise MLP activation patterns of the withheld subtype (Type 4) stay closer to its parent group (Type 2) than to control groups. This relative closeness falls once conflicting W2 supervision begins. Layer location varies by model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential fine-tuning creates and then partly dissolves relative MLP activation similarity between a parent type and a generalized subtype. This is group-level and says nothing about single-neuron monosemanticity.

record.problems: The task is a controlled synthetic integer-to-label benchmark. The authors state that the experiments provide behavioral evidence but do not directly characterize the lifted states’ representation or realization. Activation analyses are descriptive, use five seeds, and the text does not give numerical values for the plotted distances or relative-closeness curves.
record.rows_left_out: No related activation-analysis result rows were omitted. Results from the separate behavioral benchmark were left out because they do not test the neuron-focused claim versions.

untested.parts: All: audit shares across models and scale.

All: architecture and tools versus interpretability rate.
All: attribution graphs built from neurons.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper only cites neuron-level work (knowledge neurons, superposition, SAEs) as candidate bases. It makes no argument about whether neurons are clean. The activation analysis averages over neurons and layers, so it cannot speak to per-neuron interpretability.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B audit shares for one-job, two-related-job, and not-yet-understood neuron poles.
Neuron-pole audit shares across models, architectures, and scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and the proposed pose or recursive-generalization explanation.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability rates or change those rates.
Whether attribution graphs made from a model’s own neurons explain its behavior without a replacement model.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where neurons fire on independent examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by activation simulation on new text.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B
rows.operation_detail: Measured MLP neuron-wise activation-pattern distances between Type 2 and Type 4 relative to cross-control pairs during W1.
rows.measure: Proportion of cross-control distances exceeding the Type 2–Type 4 activation distance
rows.value: figure only; the text says the proportion increases during W1
rows.uncertainty: figure shows mean and standard error of the mean over five seeds
rows.note: This is a relative activation-pattern similarity result, not a measure of neuron jobs or explanation quality.
rows.check: Group-level activation-distance comparison, not a neuron-job or explanation measure. The state 'observed' has no claim version to refer to. Figure 12 shows values of about 55–85% for Qwen3-14B.
